title: What is an XRPL DestinationTag, and what does the RequireDest setting do?
abstract: Sourced guide to XRPL destination tags: what they identify, their format, the account setting that rejects untagged payments and how x402 carries them.
body:
According to the XRPL documentation, destination tags indicate the beneficiary or destination for a payment: a business that receives payments at one address can use the tag to decide which customer to credit in its own systems. [1]

In transactions, both source and destination tags are formatted as 32-bit unsigned integers. In the Payment transaction, the DestinationTag field is described as an arbitrary tag that identifies the reason for the payment to the destination, or a hosted recipient to pay. Without a tag it is not immediately obvious which customer to credit, which can require manual intervention. [1][2]

An account can enable the RequireDest setting so that the ledger rejects payments that lack a destination tag, instead of accepting money the business cannot attribute. According to the x402 exact-scheme specification for XRPL, payment requirements can carry an optional destinationTag for hosted accounts, and when it is present the signed Payment must include an equal DestinationTag. [1][3]

Author interpretation: before paying an exchange or custodian, an agent should check whether a tag is required and include it in the signed payment, because an untagged payment to a shared address may be rejected or need manual recovery. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [1][2][3]
